questions.question: Which statements about trade-offs of SLMs versus large LLMs are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: SLMs may have weaker performance on broad, complex reasoning
SLMs always outperform large models on every task
SLMs are cheaper and faster to run
SLMs can be fine-tuned effectively for narrow domains

questions.explanation: Small Language Models (SLMs) typically require less compute, memory, and cost, making them faster and cheaper to deploy. They can perform very well when fine-tuned for specific domains, but they generally do not match large frontier models on broad knowledge and complex reasoning tasks.

questions.question: A team builds a pipeline to analyze customer reviews. Which NLP preprocessing steps are typically relevant? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Converting reviews into raw electrical voltage signals
Tokenizing the text into words or subwords
Removing stop words or normalizing case where appropriate
Encoding reviews as raw uncompressed audio waveforms

questions.explanation: Common NLP preprocessing steps include tokenization, normalization, lowercasing, stemming, lemmatization, and sometimes stop-word removal. Converting text into electrical signals or audio waveforms is not part of a standard text analytics pipeline.

questions.question: An autonomous agent can execute shell commands on production systems. Which safety measures are appropriate? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Logging every action for audit and rollback
Granting unrestricted production access for speed
Requiring human approval for high-risk actions

questions.explanation: Production-grade AI agents should operate with strong guardrails, including audit logging, sandboxed execution, least-privilege access, and human approval for sensitive actions. Unrestricted production access significantly increases operational and security risks.
